name: stri_subset_regex
title: Select Elements that Match a Given Pattern

origin.description: Keep the strings that match a regular expression.
origin.usage: stri_subset_regex(str, pattern, omit_na = FALSE, negate = FALSE, ..., opts_regex = NULL)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to search.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Character vector of regular expressions. An empty pattern is not supported.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If TRUE, keep the strings that do not match.

arguments.name: opts_regex
arguments.text: A list of regex settings, or NULL for the defaults.

origin.details: A missing string or pattern, or an empty pattern, yields a missing result, and an empty pattern warns. An empty string is searched. The inputs are recycled to the longer length. pattern cannot be longer than str when str is not empty. negate flips a real match and does not flip a missing result. opts_regex holds only the settings that were supplied. Named arguments are merged into that dict and passed through stri_opts_regex. A repeated name is an error. An unknown name in a bare dict warns and is ignored. case_insensitive, comments, dotall (also dot_all), literal, multiline (also multi_line), unix_lines, and uword are ICU flags. error_on_unknown_escapes rejects an unknown backslash. time_limit and stack_limit are applied only when they are positive.
origin.value: A character vector of the kept strings.
origin.example:
result <- stri_subset_regex(c("stringi R", "123", "ID456", ""), "^[0-9]+$")
cat(paste0('stri_subset_regex(c("stringi R", "123", "ID456", ""), "^[0-9]+$") returns ', result, '.\n'))

translation.description: Keep the strings that match a regular expression.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Regular expression, missing value, or list of those. An empty pattern yields NA.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If true, keep the strings that do not match.

arguments.name: opts_regex
arguments.text: None, or a dict of only the regex settings that were supplied.

The inputs are recycled to the longer length. pattern cannot be longer than str when str is not empty. negate flips a real match and does not flip a missing result. opts_regex holds only the settings that were supplied. Named arguments are merged into that dict and passed through stri_opts_regex. A repeated name is an error. An unknown name in a bare dict warns and is ignored. case_insensitive, comments, dotall (also dot_all), literal, multiline (also multi_line), unix_lines, and uword are ICU flags. error_on_unknown_escapes rejects an unknown backslash. time_limit and stack_limit are applied only when they are positive.
translation.value: A list of the kept strings.
translation.example:
from stringi.regex import stri_subset_regex
result = stri_subset_regex(["stringi R", "123", "ID456", ""], "^[0-9]+$")
print(f'stri_subset_regex(c("stringi R", "123", "ID456", ""), "^[0-9]+$") returns {result[0]}.')
